items.summary: US military says it has destroyed three Iranian oil tankers The US military said it had struck and destroyed three oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) after US warships came under Iranian fire. "Following Iran’s failed attacks, CENTCOM permanently disabled the IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask," Central Command (Centcom) said in a statement on X. "American forces also completely destroyed the unladen crude oil carrier M/T Kylo … in the Gulf of Oman, striking the vessel in multiple critical locations to render it inoperable after the crew was directed to abandon ship," it continued. Video released by Centcom showed huge fireballs and thick plumes of flames erupting as projectiles struck the vessels. The three ships targeted were "part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies", it said. "Iran has no means by which to defend them," it added.

clusters.headline: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon

items.title: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon
items.summary: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon The price of diesel hit a new record Friday in the United States, as disruption from the US war with Iran squeezes voters. The cost is now $5.85 a gallon, up from $3.71 a year ago, the AAA motorists' association said. Diesel is used by farmers to run equipment, and it also powers the trucks needed to bring food to grocery stores. US farmers faced a double whammy of surging fertiliser and diesel prices as the spring planting season got underway. The Independent Grocers Alliance estimates that fuel-related costs can account for 15 to 30 percent of the total cost for some food products. Besides diesel, the cost of regular gasoline is also notably higher at an average of $4.15 per gallon, compared with $3.20 last year. (Reporting by AFP)

items.summary: US diesel prices hit all-time high because of Iran war Drivers in the US are paying more than ever for diesel at the pump as the US-Israeli war on Iran continues to hit ordinary citizens at home. In the US, diesel is mostly used by commercial vehicles, such as trucks, trains, boats, buses, farming vehicles and construction vehicles, the BBC reported. The average price for one gallon of diesel in the US has hit $5.85, compared to an average of $3.71 a year ago and above the previous high following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the American Automobile Association said. Fuel prices have soared since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran at the end of February, reflecting the surge in wholesale oil prices. In response to rising fuel costs, US President Donald Trump recently pledged to “substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans” through an oil deal with Venezuela, after the US kidnapped the country's former president Nicolas Maduro then supported his successor Delcy Rodriguez.

clusters.headline: Amerikaans vliegdekschip USS Abraham Lincoln verlaat Thailand

items.title: Amerikaans vliegdekschip USS Abraham Lincoln verlaat Thailand
items.summary: Het Amerikaanse vliegdekschip USS Abraham Lincoln is na vijf dagen vertrokken uit Thailand. Bijna 5000 bemanningsleden zijn meer dan negen maanden na hun vertrek uit de Verenigde Staten onderweg naar de haven van San Diego. De afgelopen vijf dagen lag de Lincoln in de Thaise haven Laem Chabang, dicht bij de badplaats Pattaya. De badplaats is Amerikaanse soldaten niet onbekend: tijdens de Vietnamoorlog werd het een bekende plek voor het zogenoemde R&R ( Rest and Relaxation) , oftewel: een vakantie voor militairen. De badplaats had daarvoor voorbereidingen getroffen: er werd onder meer een prostitutieverbod ingesteld en er werden extra agenten ingezet. "I can confirm that earlier today US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island. According to an unnamed US official cited by Al Jazeera Arabic, US forces have bombed the rocket launchers claiming they were preparing to fire missiles carrying naval mines toward the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the attack killed and wounded several soldiers and citizens and would be met with a "response and punishment" from Tehran, Iranian state media reported. US President Donald Trump ​said last week that all mines ‌had been detonated or removed from the international waters of Hormuz and Iran has been told that any ship ​or boat placing new mines will be ​destroyed. items.title: Middle East crude oil exports in August down 39 percent, TankerTrackers says
items.summary: Middle East crude oil exports in August down 39 percent, TankerTrackers says Crude oil exports out of the Middle East during August 2026 were down 39 percent since the January and February baseline of 18.5 million barrels per day (mbpd), according to oil-tracking firm TankerTrackers. The sharpest fall of 67 percent below pre-war levels was recorded in May, the firm said, adding that the current deficit is now only 7.2 mbpd, compared with 12.4 mbpd in May. The firm covered Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, Oman, the UAE and Qatar in its assessment.

items.title: Iran condemns US attacks on commercial vessels as war crimes
items.summary: Iran condemns US attacks on commercial vessels as war crimes Iran has accused the United States of violating international law by attacking its commercial vessels and imposing a naval blockade against the country. “The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the aggressive US action of attacking Iranian commercial vessels,” the Foreign Ministry said. Tehran described the strikes as part of Washington’s wider military campaign and “economic war” against Iran. It said the attacks violated the UN Charter and endangered international peace, security and commercial shipping. The ministry pledged to “firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests” against US aggression, state-sponsored terrorism, the continuing blockade and the “harassment of commercial ships”. It added that Washington and its allies would bear responsibility for any consequences arising from continued US “aggressive and interventionist actions” in the region.

items.summary: Trump says Iran war is 'small potatoes' for US Donald Trump said on Friday that the Iran war was "small potatoes" for the United States, in his administration's latest bid to play down the war ahead of crucial midterm elections. Trump's comments came a day after Vice President JD Vance said that "I wouldn't call it a war" despite an upsurge in clashes between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz. "A lot of people don't call it a war. I call it a military conflict because it's small potatoes for us," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked about Vance's remarks. "It's not a big thing. We did Venezuela, and we did this," added Trump, who was surrounded by cattle ranchers invited for the signing of two executive orders on beef processing.

clusters.headline: US, allies push IAEA board to report Iran to UN Security Council

items.title: US, allies push IAEA board to report Iran to UN Security Council
items.summary: US, allies push IAEA board to report Iran to UN Security Council The United States, Britain, France and Germany are seeking a resolution by the UN nuclear watchdog's board next week reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years, according to diplomats and the proposed text seen by Reuters. If passed, the resolution would follow up on one adopted on June 12 of last year declaring Iran in breach of its non-proliferation obligations for not fully cooperating with an investigation into uranium traces found at undeclared sites. Israel started bombing Iran's nuclear facilities the next day, soon joined by the US Iran's uranium-enrichment plants were destroyed or badly damaged. Iran has not let International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors return to the bombed sites since then or verify what remains of its stocks of enriched uranium, some of which was enriched to up to 60 percent purity, a short step from weapons grade. (Reporting by Reuters)

clusters.headline: Witkoff & Kushner to spend Labor Day weekend in Russia, Ukraine

items.title: Witkoff & Kushner to spend Labor Day weekend in Russia, Ukraine
items.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will reportedly travel to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend in an effort to revive negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. It will mark the diplomatic duo’s first trip to Kyiv since President Donald Trump’s return to office, and follows CIA director John Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow last week. “It is unclear whether the Americans are bringing new proposals to the two presidents, or are pushing them to close the gap on the remaining issues, which include who will ultimately control the Donbas, Ukrainian territory that is partly occupied by Russia,” according to a New York Times report. George Beebe, director of grand strategy at the Quincy Institute, called the development “most welcome” and said all parties had strong reasons to find a way to end the fighting. He cautioned, however, that “seizing this propitious moment will require overcoming deep mistrust between the two countries” and addressing doubt that the “Trump administration has the political clout and persistence to overcome opposition in Europe and inside the Washington establishment.”

items.title: Witkoff and Kushner to visit Russia and Ukraine at weekend, says Tass
items.summary: Witkoff and Kushner to visit Russia and Ukraine at weekend, says Tass US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Russia and Ukraine on Saturday and Sunday, Russian news agency Tass reported, citing a source. There was no immediate confirmation. Witkoff and Kushner last visited Moscow in January, when they held four hours of late-night talks with President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin, Reuters reported. The two men are also US President Donald Trump's lead negotiators on Gaza and the war on Iran. If the visit takes place it will be their first to Kyiv. “The Russians don't want them to visit Kyiv and are trying to make them change the plan,” the source told the Russian news agency. The last US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine took place in February, shortly before the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran.

clusters.headline: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?

items.title: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?
items.summary: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US? Argentina has restated its claim to sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a small rocky archipelago in the South Atlantic that is owned by the UK . Javier Milei, the far-right president of Argentina, said in a national address on Thursday that the "winds of change" favoured his country’s claim to the islands, and threatened sanctions on oil firms that seek to drill in the territory’s waters. "We need to recover these islands which are nationally relevant," he said. The announcement comes days after US President Donald Trump suggested that he is reviewing the US position on UK sovereignty, known in Argentina as Las Islas Malvinas. “I always review every position - that’s just one of many,” Trump told reporters in the White House. “The UK’s got some problems, but they’ll get solved." The future of the sparsely inhabited islands has been speculated on for months amid tensions between Washington and London about UK military commitments, including the war on Iran . items.title: De un chalé de Arturo Soria a un polígono de Villaverde: viaje a las religiones que menos fieles profesan en Madrid
items.summary: Está lejos, Amritsar. Miles de kilómetros separan la capital española de esta ciudad de la India, en la que se levanta el corazón espiritual del sijismo, una religión nacida de un acercamiento de posturas entre el hinduismo y el islam. Cada día, los sij de esta región se reúnen para comer en la monumental infraestructura que constituye el Templo Dorado, donde llenan sus bandejas sin coste ni distinción por edad, género o religión. Lo mismo sucede, en proporciones contenidas, en una nave industrial de Villaverde que esconde el único templo sij de la capital, el Gurudwara Nanaksar Sahib de Madrid. Con el mismo espíritu que en la India, pero en esplendor y dimensiones reducidos, este lugar ofrece comidas gratuitas cada domingo a unas pocas decenas de personas.Laura, madrileña de Las Rozas y bautizada en el catolicismo, es una habitual en el lugar desde que, hace más de un año, un viaje a la India despertó en ella una nueva forma de concebir su fe. «Aquí aprendo cómo llegar a dios, que es el mismo para todos», sostiene. items.summary: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports The Pentagon has begun subjecting senior military officials to lie-detector tests as part of an investigation into who leaked details about US munitions stockpiles, US media reported. Reports in July said the US was rationing some munitions, particularly missile interceptors, amid concerns over supplies following months of war with Iran. Trump administration officials strongly rejected the claims. President Donald Trump said the US had "a lot of ammunition, different types", while acknowledging that the military would like more of "some of the more sophisticated stuff". The New York Times reported late on Friday that around 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff, the Pentagon’s planning and advisory body, were being required to undergo polygraph tests as part of an investigation into the leak.

items.summary: Het plotselinge vertrek van een prominente Fox News-presentator wekt verbazing in de VS. Mogelijk spelen te nauwe banden met de regering-Trump een rol. Bartiromo zelf heeft nog niet over haar vertrek gesproken. Op haar X-account en website staat nog steeds dat ze bij Fox werkt. Bartiromo had twee populaire shows bij Fox: Mornings with Maria en Maria Bartiromo's Wall Street . Beide programma's worden overgenomen door een roulerend team van presentatoren, onder de namen Mornings with Fox Business Network en FBN's Wall Street . Trump-connectie Bartiromo onderhield nauw contact met president Trump. Ze was een van de eersten die hem interviewden na zijn vertrek uit het Witte Huis in 2021. clusters.headline: ‘The noise was unbelievable’: the referee’s view of Mexico v England at the World Cup

items.title: ‘The noise was unbelievable’: the referee’s view of Mexico v England at the World Cup
items.summary: England’s manager Thomas Tuchel called the officiating ‘just not good enough’ in the fiery last-16 tie. Now Alireza Faghani gives his version of events It was 6pm on 5 July in Mexico City, and Alireza Faghani, a 48-year-old Australian-Iranian, was asleep in the locker room, snoring. His assistants had turned the music down. Had it not been for the muffled roar of nearly 90,000 fans through the concrete walls of the Estadio Azteca, he could have slept until the following morning. Faghani was the referee for Mexico v England in the last 16 at the 2026 World Cup. Mexico hadn’t lost a competitive game at the Azteca since 2013, at least in part because they’re used to the conditions. Situated 2,240 metres above sea level, the air contains less oxygen. Opponents struggle to breathe, let alone win. Continue reading...

items.summary: Kpler says Hormuz traffic dropped sharply on 31 August, Bab el-Mandeb stable Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell sharply on August 31, with five confirmed crossings, down 50 percent from 10 a day earlier, according to maritime data firm Kpler. Four vessels entered the Middle East Gulf and one exited, using a mix of Iranian, Omani and negotiated routes. Two of the crossings involved shadow vessels, while one involved a sanctioned vessel. Kpler said the figure remained preliminary, noting that additional “dark” crossings could be retrospectively identified and added as new confirmation data becomes available. Activity through the Bab el-Mandeb was comparatively stable, with 35 confirmed crossings, up 2.9 percent day on day. Nineteen vessels entered the Red Sea and 16 exited. No dark transits were recorded, while the International Maritime Organization verified no additional attacks. The move is the latest in the Trump administration's campaign to economically pressure Tehran six months into Washington's war on Iran, which has pushed energy prices higher worldwide. Diesel prices at home in the US are at an all-time high. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who last month announced an “economic onslaught” against Iran's financial links around the world, has said Washington is seeking to force Tehran back to the negotiating table, Reuters reported.

clusters.headline: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN

items.title: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN
items.summary: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN World food prices rose in August to their highest since late 2022, impacted partly by the war on Iran, the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Friday. Extreme heat and drought in Europe, the threat of a severe El Nino weather pattern and trade upheaval caused by the Ukraine and Iran wars have unsettled agricultural markets, pushing grain prices to three-year highs and sugar to a one-year peak, the agency said. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 133.3 points in August, up from July's revised reading of 130.8. That was the highest score since November 2022, though nearly 17 percent below a record peak from March 2022, after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Reuters reported. Escalating attacks in the Black Sea have curtailed grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine, while the war on Iran is still straining flows of fertiliser for crops.

items.summary: Adam Telle appointed as acting US Army Secretary, Trump says US President Donald Trump said that he was appointing Adam Telle, assistant secretary of the Army for civil works, as the acting US Army Secretary. This came after the White House confirmed earlier this week that former army secretary, Dan Driscoll, submitted his resignation. Driscoll’s departure came following reports of increasing tensions with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth as well as signs of unease in the Pentagon over how the Trump administration is prosecuting the war on Iran. The heads of the army, navy and air force, and the four-star commanders overseeing US operations throughout Europe, Asia and Latin America, have warned Hegseth that any prolonging of major operations would weaken the Washington's ability to confront other foes, the Washington Post reported on Monday.

Iran exported about 90 percent of its crude oil from the island before the war.

items.summary: As the Trump administration refuses to end its war in Iran, it is steering into the storm, not out of it Russia hasn’t yet killed large numbers of Europeans outside Ukraine, but it’s getting closer. The night of 4-5 August, an airport bus driver discovered an armed drone lying near the tarmac of the Leipzig-Halle airport, which is a central hub of Europe’s logistical support to Ukraine’s war effort. A cargo jet, meanwhile, may have struck a second drone shortly after takeoff, forcing an abrupt landing, and investigators found a third drone laden with military explosives nearby. In 2024, incendiary devices hidden in parcels ignited in DHL cargo at the same airport. Had these detonated in the air, a major air catastrophe and large-scale civilian casualties would have ensued, probably resulting in a broader war. Continue reading...

clusters.headline: ‘I would rather die than return to France’: the brutal reality of the UK’s one in, one out scheme

items.title: ‘I would rather die than return to France’: the brutal reality of the UK’s one in, one out scheme
items.summary: Aso and Baran fled Iran, crossed the Channel together and were both returned to France. After risking their lives to reach Britain again, the friends found themselves facing very different fates At the end of last year, two men fled Iran. Aso and Baran* were strangers at the time. The way their stories would cross, then diverge, reveals the cruel arbitrariness of the UK asylum system in general, and the government’s controversial one in, one out scheme in particular. Before he left Iran, Aso, 28, had converted from Islam to Christianity, putting his life in imminent danger. “I had to keep my conversion to Christianity a secret,” he says. “I knew if I was caught, I risked being executed by the Iranian regime … one of my relatives, who I trusted, paid smugglers to get me out last November.” Continue reading...

clusters.headline: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran

items.title: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran
items.summary: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said it "wouldn't be appropriate to say" if he would greenlight the CIA arming Iranians to encourage a violent uprising, a day after he asked on his TruthSocial account, "When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?" Trump was taking unscheduled questions in the Oval Office, after the US unleashed a barrage of strikes on Iran's southern coast on Tuesday, killing 18 people, including two children at a wedding. "Will you send the CIA in to arm Iranians?" a reporter asked the president. "I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say," Trump responded. "But I mean, I understand their plight. They're being shot... They have close to 65,000 protesters killed." It remains unclear where that figure is sourced, given Trump has previously floated figures between 25,000 and 80,000 during the anti-government protests in Iran early this year. items.title: Trump’s Saudi nuke agreement may prolong the Iran war
items.summary: A final deal between the United States and Iran is slipping further out of reach. Since the Memorandum of Understanding collapsed in July, the prospects for reviving it have deteriorated by the day. While Tehran publicly demands a return to the MOU, Trump’s current position is that even if Iran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, he would neither return to the agreement nor lift the blockade on Iran. And even in the unlikely event that he did, the MOU could not come back into force as long as Israel continues to bombard Lebanon. Iran is unlikely to accept an MOU minus Lebanon: its demand for a regional ceasefire is non-negotiable. But even if these obstacles were resolved, profound differences over the nuclear issue would remain. And those differences have now grown dramatically more severe because of Trump’s nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia. Tuesday’s spike in gilt yields, taking the UK’s 30-year borrowing costs to their highest level since 1998 , was part of an international sell-off of government debt . The main contributors are well known. The Iran war, by increasing the cost of energy, has overturned the comforting start-of-the-year thesis of falling global inflation and interest rates. A plunging Japanese yen has kicked away another assumed source of financial stability. The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, hasn’t calmed nerves with his solo, and so far futile, attempt to bring down US yields . items.summary: Het Nationaal Warmtefonds heeft tot nu toe al meer leningen verstrekt dan in heel 2025. Bij het fonds kunnen mensen geld lenen om hun huis te verduurzamen. Van januari tot en met augustus werden ruim 22.000 leningen verstrekt. In heel 2025 waren dat er 21.000. De lening wordt gebruikt voor bijvoorbeeld muur- en dakisolatie, isolerend glas of zonnepanelen. De piek heeft te maken met de oorlog in het Midden-Oosten, die de VS en Israël eind februari ontketenden met hun aanvallen op Iran. Als tegenzet gooide Iran de Straat van Hormuz dicht, de zeestraat waardoor tot die tijd een vijfde van de wereldwijde olie en aardgas werd vervoerd. Door die blokkade zijn de energieprijzen fors gestegen. "De piek was vanaf het moment dat de oorlog begon", vertelt Katinka Huiberts, bestuurslid bij het Nationaal Warmtefonds. "De aanvragen begonnen toen heel scherp te stijgen." Die stijging zette het hele voorjaar tot de zomer door, zegt Huiberts. items.summary: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigned this week, raising a flurry of questions about whether his departure is part of a larger political reordering that has pushed skeptics of President Donald Trump’s war policies to the margins. A long-time friend of Vice President JD Vance, Driscoll drew widespread praise for his efforts to modernize the Army. But he has clashed with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, particularly over the latter’s firing of numerous senior military officials , including Army and Air Force generals and the Secretary of the Navy. Driscoll brought his concerns about these firings directly to Trump last week, who said he was unaware of how many officers had been purged, according to the Atlantic. clusters.headline: Gulf states struggle to recover economically after 6 months of war

items.title: Gulf states struggle to recover economically after 6 months of war
items.summary: The Persian Gulf’s extraordinary wealth has long rested on an assumption of stability. The past six months of war have shattered that certainty, exposing a fundamental weakness in Gulf economic models: producing oil and gas is only half the equation when infrastructure and access to global markets can be disrupted. Ports, airports, power grids, desalination plants, financial centers, and tourism hubs are all vulnerable to the same regional shocks. The energy sector is particularly exposed, with damaged oil and gas facilities potentially taking months or longer to repair. Yet restoring production may prove easier than restoring confidence that Gulf exports can reliably reach global markets. Each Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) state enters this new era from a different starting point. Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain are particularly exposed because of their reliance on Gulf maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz. items.summary: The signing on 7 August of the so-called Mecca Pact by Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan again raises the question of whether the Gulf monarchies might seek to reduce their security dependence on the United States. The Gulf monarchies’ experience of the Iran war makes such a realignment appear plausible. Despite their decades-long partnership with Washington, they became targets of Iranian drone and missile attacks that caused considerable damage to the region’s energy infrastructure and severely disrupted energy exports, as the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed. The Trump administration appears to have taken little account of their security interests . Nevertheless, three factors make an end to their close ties with Washington unlikely. Limits of realignment First, the Gulf monarchies have no viable alternative to the United States as a security guarantor. For all their differences in foreign and security policy, they share a common predicament: None of their other partners is willing or able to take Washington’s place. The Trump administration also tacitly endorsed a multilateral, Saudi-led maritime initiative to protect shipping in the Red Sea, sending senior U.S. military officials to the meeting where the arrangement was agreed to. The thread running through both initiatives is clear: regional states taking greater responsibility for their own security. items.title: La modernité de l’Iranienne Forough Farrokhzâd, poétesse rebelle et lumineuse
items.summary: Forough Farrokhzâd est l’une des plus grandes figures de la poésie iranienne du dernier siècle. Sa disparition brutale en 1967, à l’âge de 32 ans, fut une perte immense pour son pays, pour la littérature. Sa voix, « fusionnée dans les atomes du temps » comme elle l’a écrit, continue de se faire entendre à travers sa poésie sublime et tragique. « J’irai jusqu’au rivage du soleil » est le titre du volume en traduction française de ses poésies complètes, paru cette année dans la prestigieuse collection Poésie/Gallimard.

The restrictions would continue until US military actions against Iran end and relevant commitments are implemented, it said on Saturday in a statement. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi also reiterated that Hormuz remains closed and that Tehran is in no hurry to reopen it, Iran's Student News Network (SNN) reported. He said Iran and Oman had reached an understanding on arrangements for passage through the strait, but stressed that it would depend on the US fulfilling its commitments.

clusters.headline: Iran-backed Iraqi group sets 10 conditions for disarmament, including full US withdrawal

items.title: Iran-backed Iraqi group sets 10 conditions for disarmament, including full US withdrawal
items.summary: Iran-backed Iraqi group sets 10 conditions for disarmament, including full US withdrawal Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada, an Iran -backed Iraqi armed group, said on Saturday it will only cooperate with efforts to bring weapons under state control if 10 conditions are met, including a complete withdrawal of US forces from Iraq. The group said US forces must fully withdraw by land, sea and air, that any American presence “under any title” must end, and that Iraqi airspace must not be used to launch attacks on neighbouring countries. It also called for full federal control over Iraqi territory, stronger Iraqi-operated air defences with advanced systems, and the withdrawal of Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) fighters and Turkish troops from northern Iraq. It said that the PKK's presence gives Turkey a pretext for cross-border operations. The group, which has longstanding ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), made its statement as the Iraqi government faces a 30 September deadline to bring all armed factions' weapons under state control.

Whether Scott Bessent will achieve similar posterity as the face of the “economic D-day” in Iran remains to be seen. The US treasury secretary, already trying to manage a $40tn national debt pile, this week took charge of Donald Trump ’s effort to reverse-engineer his war of choice. items.title: The rebranding of ‘Lake America’ is Trump’s desperate attempt to distract us | Arwa Mahdawi
items.summary: Ignore Iran, the Epstein files, and your wallet – not to mention Trump’s plummeting approval ratings Don’t mention the war! Or the economy, for that matter. Or the Epstein files. Or Natalie Harp. Or “affordability”, which, as Donald Trump recently said at a rally, is a word that was “never used” by the media before he took office. Best not to talk about anything that affects ordinary people or embarrasses the president, really. Instead, let’s all rejoice in Trump’s latest triumph: renaming Lake Ontario, which is shared by Canada and the US, as Lake America . On Thursday, Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to America-fy the lake’s name on US maps and documents, which is an excellent use of time and resources. I suppose we can at least be thankful that the president, who is trying to slap his own name on everything from airports to the Kennedy Center , didn’t decree that the body of water be called Lake Trump. items.title: Nog 400 schepen vast in Perzische Golf, Iran claimt controle over Straat van Hormuz
items.summary: Sinds het begin van de Iranoorlog een half jaar geleden liggen nog altijd 400 schepen vast in de Perzische Golf. Dat meldt de Internationale Maritieme Organisatie (IMO). Ook zitten nog 6000 opvarenden vast, zegt de organisatie. "Zes maanden na het begin van het conflict in het Midden-Oosten is de situatie in de Straat van Hormuz nog steeds onopgelost", aldus IMO's secretaris-generaal Arsenio Dominguez. De wereldwijde economische impact door verstoringen van handelsstromen voor olie, kunstmest en andere grondstoffen door de blokkade is groot, zegt Dominguez. Sinds het begin van het conflict noteerde de IMO minstens zeventig aanvallen op de internationale scheepvaart met negentien doden tot gevolg. De IMO-raad nam vorige maand een resolutie aan waarin wordt opgeroepen tot een "gecoördineerde en duurzame terugkeer naar onbelemmerde navigatie door de Straat van Hormuz". clusters.headline: Ghalibaf says 'no one will be able to sell oil in region where Iran can't'

items.title: Ghalibaf says 'no one will be able to sell oil in region where Iran can't'
items.summary: Ghalibaf says 'no one will be able to sell oil in region where Iran can't' Iran’s parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has warned that “no one will be able to sell oil in a region where Tehran cannot”, according to Mehr News Agency. On Friday, Ghalibaf republished on X a message originally dated 22 July, responding to earlier claims by US Central Command (Centcom) commander Admiral Brad Cooper that American forces had achieved full control of the Strait of Hormuz and halted Iran's oil exports. “The equation of this war is clear: either all or none!” he said. “In a region where we don’t sell oil, no one else will sell oil either.” He also said that the security of the Strait of Hormuz, lies in “the absence” of US troops. “If our security is not ensured, no infrastructure will be safe,” he said, according to Mehr.

clusters.headline: Iran will neither forgive nor forget Minab school massacre, Araghchi says

items.title: Iran will neither forgive nor forget Minab school massacre, Araghchi says
items.summary: Iran will neither forgive nor forget Minab school massacre, Araghchi says Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has said that his country will neither forgive nor forget the Minab school massacre “but will continue to pursue it”, IRNA reported. During a visit to the “Minab School” painting exhibition on Friday, Araghchi said human rights have “become a political tool in the hands of some Western states”, “exploiting them for political gain and attaching no real value to the concept”. “We believe in human rights in the true sense of the word in Iran and have always defended the rights of the Iranian people and will not allow it to be abused by others,” he added, according to IRNA. In February, a double strike on a girls' school in Minab in southern Iran killed 165 people, mostly students aged seven to 12. Local officials say about 170 girls were at the school during the attack, which Iran attributes to the US and Israel.

items.summary: US cuts off major Egyptian bank from global financial system The US Treasury on Friday announced plans to cut off Banque Misr's branches in the United Arab Emirates from the global financial system, as the Trump administration seeks to "asphyxiate" what it said were Iran's "enablers". Banque Misr is Egypt's second-largest bank. Its Emirati arm will no longer be able to do business in US dollars as of 28 September, under the new plans. The 30-day notification period is open for public comment, a process whereby the US government solicits messages of support or opposition that could potentially sway the decision. "The US Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) proposed a rule that would revoke Banque Misr UAE’s correspondent banking access to US financial institutions. Treasury assesses that Banque Misr UAE is a critical node for the Iranian regime’s access to U.S. dollars," the Treasury said. items.summary: This week, President Donald Trump formally submitted the U.S.-Saudi civil nuclear agreement to Congress for review, moving the deal forward despite continuing to insist that Saudi Arabia normalize relations with Israel before it can take effect. This condition could stall the agreement indefinitely: Riyadh demands a clear pathway toward Palestinian statehood before normalization, and Israel is dead set against statehood. Israel had strongly opposed the deal as originally negotiated, while Netanyahu had privately expressed hopes of delivering “ the next big thing ” by securing Saudi normalization before Israel’s October elections. Former U.S. Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Michael Ratney described Trump as inserting normalization “ at the last minute ,” throwing the agreement into uncertainty. Trump’s decision to submit the agreement for congressional review further adds to this uncertainty. The president appears to want it both ways: his latest move is signaling to Riyadh that the agreement is moving forward even as he assures Tel Aviv that the deal is contingent on normalization. items.summary: Hormuz traffic drops to lowest since May An average of 10 commodity ships transited the Strait of Hormuz daily over the past 10 days, marking the lowest traffic in the waterway since May, shipping data by Kpler on Monday showed. Rezaei says Tehran has started activating overland trade corridors to reduce its dependence on shipping and counter the maritime blockade. He pointed to Iran’s borders with 15 neighbouring countries, arguing that its geographical position gives it alternatives to sea-based commerce. Rezaei also said Iran and Oman had agreed on a new international corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran would oversee. “The new international corridor that Iran manages has been determined with the Omani brothers and will be announced in the coming days,” Rezaei said, according to state media.

items.title: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?
items.summary: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US? Argentina has restated its claim to sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a small rocky archipelago in the South Atlantic that is owned by the UK . Javier Milei, the far-right president of Argentina, said in a national address on Thursday that the "winds of change" favoured his country’s claim to the islands, and threatened sanctions on oil firms that seek to drill in the territory’s waters. "We need to recover these islands which are nationally relevant," he said. The announcement comes days after US President Donald Trump suggested that he is reviewing the US position on UK sovereignty, known in Argentina as Las Islas Malvinas. “I always review every position - that’s just one of many,” Trump told reporters in the White House. “The UK’s got some problems, but they’ll get solved." The future of the sparsely inhabited islands has been speculated on for months amid tensions between Washington and London about UK military commitments, including the war on Iran . Bijna 5000 bemanningsleden zijn meer dan negen maanden na hun vertrek uit de Verenigde Staten onderweg naar de haven van San Diego. De afgelopen vijf dagen lag de Lincoln in de Thaise haven Laem Chabang, dicht bij de badplaats Pattaya. De badplaats is Amerikaanse soldaten niet onbekend: tijdens de Vietnamoorlog werd het een bekende plek voor het zogenoemde R&R ( Rest and Relaxation) , oftewel: een vakantie voor militairen. De badplaats had daarvoor voorbereidingen getroffen: er werd onder meer een prostitutieverbod ingesteld en er werden extra agenten ingezet. The renewed clashes in Yemen's southwest over control of a gateway to the Red Sea came after Friday saw some of the deadliest fighting in years, following the collapse in July of a 2022 ceasefire. According to three Yemeni military sources, 26 government troops were killed during several hours of fighting in the country's southwest, while medical and military sources from the Iran-backed Houthis said 31 rebel fighters were killed. One medical source in the government-held city of Taiz said a missile strike also killed six civilians travelling by bus and wounded seven others. items.title: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports
items.summary: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports The Pentagon has begun subjecting senior military officials to lie-detector tests as part of an investigation into who leaked details about US munitions stockpiles, US media reported. Reports in July said the US was rationing some munitions, particularly missile interceptors, amid concerns over supplies following months of war with Iran. Trump administration officials strongly rejected the claims. President Donald Trump said the US had "a lot of ammunition, different types", while acknowledging that the military would like more of "some of the more sophisticated stuff". The New York Times reported late on Friday that around 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff, the Pentagon’s planning and advisory body, were being required to undergo polygraph tests as part of an investigation into the leak.

items.title: US military says it has destroyed three Iranian oil tankers
items.summary: US military says it has destroyed three Iranian oil tankers The US military said it had struck and destroyed three oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) after US warships came under Iranian fire. "Following Iran’s failed attacks, CENTCOM permanently disabled the IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask," Central Command (Centcom) said in a statement on X. "American forces also completely destroyed the unladen crude oil carrier M/T Kylo … in the Gulf of Oman, striking the vessel in multiple critical locations to render it inoperable after the crew was directed to abandon ship," it continued. Video released by Centcom showed huge fireballs and thick plumes of flames erupting as projectiles struck the vessels. The three ships targeted were "part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies", it said. "Iran has no means by which to defend them," it added.

Under the latest proposal, Tehran would be able to intervene if necessary with any inbound traffic, while outbound traffic would follow a route between Iran and Oman, with exit clearance granted through Oman after notifying Iran, a senior Iranian source told Reuters this week. Introducing compulsory charges through the strait for transit or service fees was "a toll in all but name", the world's leading shipping associations said in an open letter, which was sent to the UN's shipping agency. George Beebe, director of grand strategy at the Quincy Institute, called the development “most welcome” and said all parties had strong reasons to find a way to end the fighting. In the US, diesel is mostly used by commercial vehicles, such as trucks, trains, boats, buses, farming vehicles and construction vehicles, the BBC reported. The average price for one gallon of diesel in the US has hit $5.85, compared to an average of $3.71 a year ago and above the previous high following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the American Automobile Association said. Fuel prices have soared since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran at the end of February, reflecting the surge in wholesale oil prices. items.title: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN
items.summary: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN World food prices rose in August to their highest since late 2022, impacted partly by the war on Iran, the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Friday. Extreme heat and drought in Europe, the threat of a severe El Nino weather pattern and trade upheaval caused by the Ukraine and Iran wars have unsettled agricultural markets, pushing grain prices to three-year highs and sugar to a one-year peak, the agency said. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 133.3 points in August, up from July's revised reading of 130.8. That was the highest score since November 2022, though nearly 17 percent below a record peak from March 2022, after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Reuters reported. Escalating attacks in the Black Sea have curtailed grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine, while the war on Iran is still straining flows of fertiliser for crops.

items.title: Vance defiende el acuerdo petrolero con Venezuela como escudo ante la crisis con Irán
items.summary: Ante las dudas y críticas sobre el nuevo acuerdo petrolero de Donald Trump con Venezuela, su vicepresidente, J. D. Vance, salió este jueves en la Casa Blanca a defenderlo y a presentarlo como una pieza de la estrategia de Washington para blindar a EE.UU. frente a futuras crisis energéticas , en un momento de creciente beligerancia con Irán y de encarecimiento de los combustibles. Vance sostuvo que Washington no puede depender de que otros países garanticen el suministro mundial de energía y cargó además contra los aliados europeos, entre ellos España, por lo que describió como su incapacidad para responder con suficiente firmeza a las amenazas iraníes contra las rutas marítimas.La tesis del vicepresidente es que la apertura del sector petrolero venezolano permite a EE.UU. incorporar a los mercados una enorme reserva de crudo cercana geográficamente y reducir así la vulnerabilidad ante crisis como la actual con Irán. Según Vance, el acuerdo permitirá poner en explotación efectiva unos 65.000 millones de barriles de reservas mediante la entrada de compañías estadounidenses en Venezuela

The night of 4-5 August, an airport bus driver discovered an armed drone lying near the tarmac of the Leipzig-Halle airport, which is a central hub of Europe’s logistical support to Ukraine’s war effort. A cargo jet, meanwhile, may have struck a second drone shortly after takeoff, forcing an abrupt landing, and investigators found a third drone laden with military explosives nearby. In 2024, incendiary devices hidden in parcels ignited in DHL cargo at the same airport. Had these detonated in the air, a major air catastrophe and large-scale civilian casualties would have ensued, probably resulting in a broader war. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘I would rather die than return to France’: the brutal reality of the UK’s one in, one out scheme
items.summary: Aso and Baran fled Iran, crossed the Channel together and were both returned to France. After risking their lives to reach Britain again, the friends found themselves facing very different fates At the end of last year, two men fled Iran. Aso and Baran* were strangers at the time. The way their stories would cross, then diverge, reveals the cruel arbitrariness of the UK asylum system in general, and the government’s controversial one in, one out scheme in particular. Before he left Iran, Aso, 28, had converted from Islam to Christianity, putting his life in imminent danger. “I had to keep my conversion to Christianity a secret,” he says. “I knew if I was caught, I risked being executed by the Iranian regime … one of my relatives, who I trusted, paid smugglers to get me out last November.” Continue reading...

Darzi urged the UN to “hold the United States fully responsible” and ensure it brings “an end to its acts of aggression” against Iran. items.title: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran
items.summary: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said it "wouldn't be appropriate to say" if he would greenlight the CIA arming Iranians to encourage a violent uprising, a day after he asked on his TruthSocial account, "When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?" Trump was taking unscheduled questions in the Oval Office, after the US unleashed a barrage of strikes on Iran's southern coast on Tuesday, killing 18 people, including two children at a wedding. "Will you send the CIA in to arm Iranians?" a reporter asked the president. "I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say," Trump responded. "But I mean, I understand their plight. They're being shot... They have close to 65,000 protesters killed." It remains unclear where that figure is sourced, given Trump has previously floated figures between 25,000 and 80,000 during the anti-government protests in Iran early this year. Yet what is actually happening is that the U.S. is putting stress on an inherently flawed and now exhausted form of alliance politics. The roots of the present discord were planted not in the 2024 reelection of President Donald Trump, but in the moment of NATO's Cold War triumph thirty years earlier. items.summary: UN chief urges US, Iran to 'return urgently to diplomacy' after renewed attacks UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Wednesday expressed "grave concern" after renewed strikes between the US and Iran, and condemned all attacks against civilians. "The secretary-general is deeply alarmed by reports of civilian casualties, including a strike that reportedly hit a wedding ceremony in Iran," UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said during a news conference. "The secretary-general condemns all attacks against civilians," Dujarric said. "He recalls that all parties must respect their obligations under international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution." He added that the UN chief urged Washington and Tehran to "return urgently to diplomacy," adding that a "comprehensive and durable settlement can be achieved only through dialog and negotiations".

items.title: Trump’s Saudi nuke agreement may prolong the Iran war
items.summary: A final deal between the United States and Iran is slipping further out of reach. Since the Memorandum of Understanding collapsed in July, the prospects for reviving it have deteriorated by the day. While Tehran publicly demands a return to the MOU, Trump’s current position is that even if Iran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, he would neither return to the agreement nor lift the blockade on Iran. And even in the unlikely event that he did, the MOU could not come back into force as long as Israel continues to bombard Lebanon. Iran is unlikely to accept an MOU minus Lebanon: its demand for a regional ceasefire is non-negotiable. items.title: Oorlog Midden-Oosten leidt tot stuk meer aanvragen bij Nationaal Warmtefonds
items.summary: Het Nationaal Warmtefonds heeft tot nu toe al meer leningen verstrekt dan in heel 2025. Bij het fonds kunnen mensen geld lenen om hun huis te verduurzamen. Van januari tot en met augustus werden ruim 22.000 leningen verstrekt. In heel 2025 waren dat er 21.000. De lening wordt gebruikt voor bijvoorbeeld muur- en dakisolatie, isolerend glas of zonnepanelen. De piek heeft te maken met de oorlog in het Midden-Oosten, die de VS en Israël eind februari ontketenden met hun aanvallen op Iran. Als tegenzet gooide Iran de Straat van Hormuz dicht, de zeestraat waardoor tot die tijd een vijfde van de wereldwijde olie en aardgas werd vervoerd. Door die blokkade zijn de energieprijzen fors gestegen. "De piek was vanaf het moment dat de oorlog begon", vertelt Katinka Huiberts, bestuurslid bij het Nationaal Warmtefonds. "De aanvragen begonnen toen heel scherp te stijgen." Die stijging zette het hele voorjaar tot de zomer door, zegt Huiberts. A long-time friend of Vice President JD Vance, Driscoll drew widespread praise for his efforts to modernize the Army. But he has clashed with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, particularly over the latter’s firing of numerous senior military officials , including Army and Air Force generals and the Secretary of the Navy. Driscoll brought his concerns about these firings directly to Trump last week, who said he was unaware of how many officers had been purged, according to the Atlantic. items.summary: De adviesprijs voor een liter benzine bereikt woensdag zeer waarschijnlijk een nieuwe recordhoogte van rond de 2,668 euro. Dat bevestigt consumentencollectief UnitedConsumers na berichtgeving van nu.nl. Het oude record was van begin mei dit jaar: 2,646 euro. Vandaag steeg de prijs al naar net daaronder: 2,64 euro. Morgen stijgt de benzineprijs dus verder. UnitedConsumers berekent de gemiddelde adviesprijs dagelijks op basis van de prijzen van de vijf grote aanbieders: Shell, BP, Texaco, Esso en TotalEnergies. Vier van de vijf hebben hun prijs voor woensdag al doorgegeven. "Die vijfde gaat niet veel afwijken van de anderen, dus het record gaat er zeker aan", zegt Derk Foolen van UnitedConsumers. items.title: Gulf states struggle to recover economically after 6 months of war
items.summary: The Persian Gulf’s extraordinary wealth has long rested on an assumption of stability. The past six months of war have shattered that certainty, exposing a fundamental weakness in Gulf economic models: producing oil and gas is only half the equation when infrastructure and access to global markets can be disrupted. Ports, airports, power grids, desalination plants, financial centers, and tourism hubs are all vulnerable to the same regional shocks. The energy sector is particularly exposed, with damaged oil and gas facilities potentially taking months or longer to repair. Yet restoring production may prove easier than restoring confidence that Gulf exports can reliably reach global markets. Each Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) state enters this new era from a different starting point. Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain are particularly exposed because of their reliance on Gulf maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking on Monday before travelling to Bishkek for a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, Pezeshkian said Iran “is not looking for war” but would “never sit still in the face of any aggression”. Iran “will give a decisive response to the aggressors” if attacked again, he said, according to the Fars news agency. “Instability and unrest in the region are not in the interest of any country and will challenge everyone,” he added. US forces bombed Larak Island on Sunday, the official state broadcaster IRIB reported. It marked Washington’s first attack on Iran since July and raised fears of another escalation in the Israeli -US war against the country . items.title: Why the Gulf Monarchies Will Not Turn Away from the United States Despite the Iran War
items.summary: The signing on 7 August of the so-called Mecca Pact by Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan again raises the question of whether the Gulf monarchies might seek to reduce their security dependence on the United States. The Gulf monarchies’ experience of the Iran war makes such a realignment appear plausible. Despite their decades-long partnership with Washington, they became targets of Iranian drone and missile attacks that caused considerable damage to the region’s energy infrastructure and severely disrupted energy exports, as the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed. The Trump administration appears to have taken little account of their security interests . Nevertheless, three factors make an end to their close ties with Washington unlikely. Limits of realignment First, the Gulf monarchies have no viable alternative to the United States as a security guarantor. For all their differences in foreign and security policy, they share a common predicament: None of their other partners is willing or able to take Washington’s place. items.title: La modernité de l’Iranienne Forough Farrokhzâd, poétesse rebelle et lumineuse
items.summary: Forough Farrokhzâd est l’une des plus grandes figures de la poésie iranienne du dernier siècle. Sa disparition brutale en 1967, à l’âge de 32 ans, fut une perte immense pour son pays, pour la littérature. Sa voix, « fusionnée dans les atomes du temps » comme elle l’a écrit, continue de se faire entendre à travers sa poésie sublime et tragique. « J’irai jusqu’au rivage du soleil » est le titre du volume en traduction française de ses poésies complètes, paru cette année dans la prestigieuse collection Poésie/Gallimard.

items.title: Iran parliament speaker says new regional pacts can 'herald a new stage’
items.summary: Iran parliament speaker says new regional pacts can 'herald a new stage’ Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has said that new regional treaties can herald a new stage in which Muslim neighbours rely on their own capacities rather than on foreigners, according to Tasnim News Agency. In his message Saturday to mark the Unity Week, Ghalibaf described new regional treaties and arrangements as a “new chapter” and stressed that unity among Muslims has “helped push back against hegemonic ambitions”, according to Tasnim News Agency. He said these treaties show that Muslim neighbours “can choose the path of cooperation and brotherhood”, rather than “pursuing exhausting rivalries”. Ghalibaf added that recent developments have demonstrated the benefits of Muslim unity, and expressed hope that the Muslim world “would move toward greater unity, independence, security and dignity, with Muslims determining their own future free from foreign interference”.

items.title: Iran-backed Iraqi group sets 10 conditions for disarmament, including full US withdrawal
items.summary: Iran-backed Iraqi group sets 10 conditions for disarmament, including full US withdrawal Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada, an Iran -backed Iraqi armed group, said on Saturday it will only cooperate with efforts to bring weapons under state control if 10 conditions are met, including a complete withdrawal of US forces from Iraq. The group said US forces must fully withdraw by land, sea and air, that any American presence “under any title” must end, and that Iraqi airspace must not be used to launch attacks on neighbouring countries. It also called for full federal control over Iraqi territory, stronger Iraqi-operated air defences with advanced systems, and the withdrawal of Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) fighters and Turkish troops from northern Iraq. It said that the PKK's presence gives Turkey a pretext for cross-border operations. The group, which has longstanding ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), made its statement as the Iraqi government faces a 30 September deadline to bring all armed factions' weapons under state control.

Or Natalie Harp. Or “affordability”, which, as Donald Trump recently said at a rally, is a word that was “never used” by the media before he took office. Best not to talk about anything that affects ordinary people or embarrasses the president, really. Instead, let’s all rejoice in Trump’s latest triumph: renaming Lake Ontario, which is shared by Canada and the US, as Lake America . On Thursday, Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to America-fy the lake’s name on US maps and documents, which is an excellent use of time and resources. Ook zitten nog 6000 opvarenden vast, zegt de organisatie. "Zes maanden na het begin van het conflict in het Midden-Oosten is de situatie in de Straat van Hormuz nog steeds onopgelost", aldus IMO's secretaris-generaal Arsenio Dominguez. De wereldwijde economische impact door verstoringen van handelsstromen voor olie, kunstmest en andere grondstoffen door de blokkade is groot, zegt Dominguez. Sinds het begin van het conflict noteerde de IMO minstens zeventig aanvallen op de internationale scheepvaart met negentien doden tot gevolg. De IMO-raad nam vorige maand een resolutie aan waarin wordt opgeroepen tot een "gecoördineerde en duurzame terugkeer naar onbelemmerde navigatie door de Straat van Hormuz". During a visit to the “Minab School” painting exhibition on Friday, Araghchi said human rights have “become a political tool in the hands of some Western states”, “exploiting them for political gain and attaching no real value to the concept”. “We believe in human rights in the true sense of the word in Iran and have always defended the rights of the Iranian people and will not allow it to be abused by others,” he added, according to IRNA. In February, a double strike on a girls' school in Minab in southern Iran killed 165 people, mostly students aged seven to 12. Local officials say about 170 girls were at the school during the attack, which Iran attributes to the US and Israel.

This condition could stall the agreement indefinitely: Riyadh demands a clear pathway toward Palestinian statehood before normalization, and Israel is dead set against statehood. Israel had strongly opposed the deal as originally negotiated, while Netanyahu had privately expressed hopes of delivering “ the next big thing ” by securing Saudi normalization before Israel’s October elections. Former U.S. Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Michael Ratney described Trump as inserting normalization “ at the last minute ,” throwing the agreement into uncertainty. Trump’s decision to submit the agreement for congressional review further adds to this uncertainty. The president appears to want it both ways: his latest move is signaling to Riyadh that the agreement is moving forward even as he assures Tel Aviv that the deal is contingent on normalization.
